investigated_sources_inventory.name: Abisko Valley Floor Ceilometer / All-Sky Camera
investigated_sources_inventory.operator: SITES / CIRC / Swedish Polar Research Secretariat
investigated_sources_inventory.location: ANS Valley Floor (68.3532 N, 18.8164 E, 388m ASL)
investigated_sources_inventory.archive_2024_status: Campaign research archive only; no operational NRT pipeline
investigated_sources_inventory.spatial_representativeness: Poor (Valley inversion layer decouples 388m valley from 920m summit)

investigated_sources_inventory.name: Abisko Valley Floor Surface Radiation (Direct/Diffuse)

investigated_sources_inventory.name: SMHI / MET Norway Upwind SYNOP Stations (Katterjåkk, Narvik)
investigated_sources_inventory.spatial_representativeness: Valley surface weather does not capture column cloud optical depth; separated by Scandes ridge
investigated_sources_inventory.redundancy_assessment: High (Already assimilated into MEPS 18Z initial state)

investigated_sources_inventory.name: Regional SWEPOS GNSS Stations (KIRU, JALL, PAJA, TRO1)

investigated_sources_inventory.name: GNSS 3D Tropospheric Tomography / Slant Path Water Vapour

investigated_sources_inventory.classification: CLOSED — INSUFFICIENT COVERAGE (<45% valid causal coverage before t0; fails polar night)

evidence_gaps_summary: No operational NRT ground-based cloud radar, ceilometer, or microwave radiometer exists at Abisko Nuolja.
Geostationary satellite retrievals (SEVIRI) suffer 20.9 km parallax displacement at 68.35 N and fail 90% coverage gate (70.11%).
Polar-orbiting satellite overpasses occur at irregular times, providing valid causal data before t0 on < 45% of days.
Upwind radiosondes and regional SYNOP stations are 195-335 km distant and fully assimilated into MEPS/AROME initial conditions.
Downwind GNSS stations (Kiru, Jall, Paja) decorrelate from mountain moisture and provide zero upwind predictive lead time.
